actual_source_values.alignment_requirement: Reliable segment start/end transfer is sufficient; frame-perfect alignment and per-sample timestamps are not required. No independently documented start offset/drift or segment anchor was found in available evidence.
actual_source_values.decoding_evidence: Reuse prior full-stream decoding and per-segment checks from immutable inventory; raw sizes/mtime and audited-record hashes verified. Header inspection repeated now; no new audio payload cache.
actual_source_values.decision: AUDIO NOT INCLUDED — SEGMENT-ALIGNMENT OR COVERAGE PRECONDITION FAILED
actual_source_values.reason: Nominal origin is inferred from the earliest non-audio timestamp, not a measured audio clock mapping. Decoder-reported and actually decoded sample counts can disagree. Nominal overlap does not establish correct action-segment association.

action_clock: Absolute Unix-style timestamps stored in segments_info start/end; video and robot_state are indexed with their timestamps datasets. Hardware clock provenance is not independently established here.
nominal_audio_origin: Inventory nominal_audio_origin: minimum first timestamp across available non-audio timestamp arrays (src/reassemble/inventory.py). This is an inferred origin, not an audio-to-annotation clock calibration.
why_unverified: No audio timestamp arrays or dataset clock attributes establish an independently documented offset, drift correction, or action-segment anchor. Header sample counts can disagree with decoded counts. A zero-based decoded sample clock plus an assumed recording origin cannot verify action identity.
why_excluded: Nominal overlap measures coverage under an assumed origin; it does not prove label-safe extraction of each completed action. Audio was excluded by the timing/coverage prerequisite, not by a predictive-model result.
illustration_rule: Central 10 seconds of each full decoded stream of the lexicographically first selected recording, independent of action timing; no exported audio files.
